short: Convolutional denoising AE features (M06) are standard: denoising and CNN features predate it; DCT margin 0.21-0.41 points (2-4 of 1023 words), one speaker, runs unstated.
position: The paper [@li2019denoising] changes one component, the ultrasound feature extractor (M06), replacing DCT or a fully connected autoencoder with a convolutional autoencoder trained on speckle-corrupted inputs; it is standard. Both halves predate it, speckle denoising of tongue ultrasound [@jaumardhakoun2016articulatory] and CNN features from raw tongue ultrasound [@tatulli2017feature], so the "first attempt" (§4) holds only for their combination. The headline 6.17% against the "state-of-the-art" 6.45% (Abstract) sets length 60 against DCT at length 30; at equal length the margin is 0.41 points at length 60 and 0.21 at length 30, about 4 and 2 words of the 1023-word test [@ji2018updating] (inference), on one speaker with the number of runs not reported. Denoising adds 0.05 points over the plain CAE (Table 2): the evidence supports convolution, not denoising. The eight new WERs in Table 2 are not whole error counts over 1023 words, while the two that equal Ji et al.'s published values are (inference), and the paper does not say why.
